title: You Can't Win an Argument
coreMove: Notice the moment you are about to prove someone wrong, and step out of the argument before the win costs you the person.

exampleSpecs.domain: a line cook on a Friday dinner rush correcting a new dishwasher who keeps stacking sauté pans wrong
exampleSpecs.audience: a 34-year-old sous chef who came up under shouters and is trying not to become one
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the dishwasher quits before Saturday brunch and leaves the line short-handed for the weekend
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the cook wins the point about pan stacking, watches the dishwasher's face go flat, and realizes he has just traded a competent worker for being right about steel

exampleSpecs.domain: a pediatric night-shift nurse and a sleep-deprived father disagreeing over whether his eighteen-month-old's fever needs the ER
exampleSpecs.audience: a nurse with twelve years on the floor talking to a first-time parent at 2 a.m.
exampleSpecs.stakes: the father's trust in the hospital for the rest of a long admission, and whether he listens to the discharge instructions in the morning
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse drops her clinically correct rebuttal mid-sentence, asks the father what he is most afraid of, and lets his answer reshape what she says next

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school debate coach watching her best student demolish an opponent at a regional tournament
exampleSpecs.audience: a teacher in her late forties who used to compete herself
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether her star learns to persuade adults outside the gym or only to crush peers inside it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coach hears applause for a clean rhetorical kill and quietly admits she has been training a winner who nobody at home wants to talk to anymore

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional sales manager defending a soft quarterly forecast to a CFO who is already drafting a layoff memo
exampleSpecs.audience: a manager who is technically right about the numbers and politically about to lose
exampleSpecs.stakes: his territory's headcount and his own credibility for the next two quarters
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he chooses to concede the CFO's framing out loud first, in plain English, before laying out his own figures, and feels the room change temperature

exampleSpecs.domain: a divorced father arguing with his fifteen-year-old daughter about a curfew her mother already approved
exampleSpecs.audience: a dad who gets her every other weekend and is afraid of becoming the strict house
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether she tells him anything real about her life for the next year
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: replaying the kitchen scene, he sees the exact sentence where he won the curfew and lost the conversation, and writes down what he wishes he had said instead

exampleSpecs.domain: a condo board treasurer who spots a retired neighbor's arithmetic error on the reserve fund during the annual meeting
exampleSpecs.audience: a treasurer who is correct, in public, in front of fifty neighbors
exampleSpecs.stakes: the retiree's standing on the board and whether anyone speaks up at the next meeting
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the treasurer catches the error, pauses, and chooses a private hallway correction over the satisfying public one, then watches the retiree volunteer the fix himself a week later
